payload.subject: Mathematics
payload.lesson_type_evidence: imagine you have 3 bananas and you get 2 more bananas from the kitchen. How many bananas do you have now? You can count them together like this: 3, 4, 5.
learning_objectives: Students will be able to add two single-digit numbers using concrete objects.
Students will be able to represent addition situations with pictures and symbols.
learning_outcomes: Students will solve real‑life addition problems with objects and drawings.
Students will write correct addition sentences for given situations.
misconceptions: Students may think that addition always results in a larger number without considering zero.
Students may confuse the plus (+) and minus (−) signs.
suggested_instructional_sequence: Begin with a story problem using bananas or apples.
Use physical objects to model the problem.
Draw pictures to represent the objects.
Introduce the addition symbol and equal sign.
